panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Real patient renal biopsy H&E at low power from the index MPA case; shows glomerular and tubulointerstitial involvement consistent with the diagnosed pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis of microscopic polyangiitis. B: PAS-stained glomerulus from the same MPA patient showing a cellular crescent, the classic renal lesion of microscopic polyangiitis; disease attribution is explicit in the caption and in-text diagnosis. C: Silver-stained glomerulus from the MPA case clearly demonstrates crescentic glomerular injury, matching the pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis that is the hallmark renal manifestation of microscopic polyangiitis. D: Masson's trichrome highlights fibrinoid necrosis and crescent formation in a glomerulus of the MPA patient, confirming necrotizing crescentic (pauci-immune) glomerulonephritis, the classic renal expression of microscopic polyangiitis.

panels.rationale: Single-panel Jones methenamine silver renal biopsy from a patient with MPO-ANCA microscopic polyangiitis (disease-focused article title and prior caption triage). The image visibly shows a glomerulus with fibrinoid necrosis and early crescent formation in the urinary space, i.e. necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis, a classic renal manifestation of microscopic polyangiitis; the in-text phrase 'necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis' is a listed synonym of the vocabulary finding. Confidence is moderated because the in-text notes 'significant IgA deposits (not shown in figure)', which tempers a strictly pauci-immune interpretation, but the silver-stain morphology itself and the article/prior-triage attribution support microscopic polyangiitis. in_text_mentions: A renal biopsy was performed, with evidence of intraglomerular thrombi, fibrinoid necrosis with neutrophilic granulocyte infiltrate and fibrocellular crescents; tubular atrophy and presence of intratubular hyaline cylinders. Interstitial mild edema was also observed alongside a moderate inflammatory infiltrate in the periglomerular area consisting of small lymphocytes (CD3 +/−, CD20 −/+), neutrophil granulocytes, histiocytes (CD 68+) and some plasma cells. These findings were consistent with microscopic polyangiitis, with features of micro-thrombotic glomerulopathy (Fig. 1).

panels.rationale: Frontal chest radiograph from a patient with microscopic polyangiitis showing bilateral patchy infiltrates, consistent with the pulmonary manifestation of MPA (diffuse alveolar hemorrhage secondary to pulmonary capillaritis). Disease attribution rests on the disease-focused article title ('A Rare Case of SARS-CoV-2-Induced Microscopic Polyangiitis') together with the specific captioned manifestation. Confidence is moderated because the patient also had SARS-CoV-2 infection, which can itself produce bilateral patchy infiltrates, and because the radiographic finding is non-specific; the caption does not explicitly state alveolar hemorrhage. The finding key 'diffuse alveolar hemorrhage' is the closest vocabulary match for the radiographic appearance, though the vocabulary entry is categorized for CT.
